info.title: tasmota-power
info.description: Multi-driver smart plug control and energy monitoring per printer (Tasmota, Shelly Gen1/Gen2+, Zigbee2MQTT, ESPHome, OpenBeken, Generic MQTT, and Home Assistant).

get.summary: Get the connection settings and their live state
get.description: Returns the MQTT broker and Home Assistant settings with secrets left out, whether each connection is up, the state of the built-in broker and whether its port is granted, and which values are pinned by the host's own settings.

200.description: Current MQTT settings and broker status

put.description: Replaces the whole settings object in settings.json and reconnects the MQTT broker. A value pinned in the host's own settings is kept as pinned.

200.description: Updated MQTT settings and broker status

post.description: Tests connecting to the provided (or saved) external or built-in MQTT broker settings and returns whether the connection succeeded or the exact error. The built-in broker is tested on the port the operator granted.

post.summary: Test Home Assistant REST connectivity and list switch/power entities
post.description: Tests connecting to the provided (or saved) Home Assistant URL and Long-Lived Access Token via GET /api/ and returns discovered switch, input_boolean, and power sensor entities.

200.description: Home Assistant test result and entity list

post.summary: Ask the MQTT broker which plugs are there
post.description: Queries the broker for Tasmota and Shelly Gen1 plugs and returns every plug found.

get.summary: List every printer's plug and the plugs the broker found
get.description: Returns each printer's saved plug, the plugs the broker found, the Home Assistant entities, and the state of both connections.

200.description: All printer plug assignments and discovered plugs

get.summary: List every printer's plug and what it draws now
get.description: Returns, for every printer the caller may see that has a plug or an auto-off choice, the saved plug with secrets left out, its live state and readings, and the energy since it was turned on. It reads memory only, so one request serves a whole list of printers.

200.description: Every visible printer's plug, and the state of both connections

get.summary: Get one printer's plug, its live state, its power graph and its safety lock
get.description: Returns the printer's saved plug, live relay and power readings, rolling power graph samples, session and per-print energy totals, the active-print safety lock, and the auto-off countdown.

200.description: Device power plug status and energy usage telemetry

put.summary: Save one printer's plug and its auto-off choices
put.description: Saves the driver, the plug's address (an MQTT topic, an IP address or host, a Home Assistant entity, or custom MQTT topics), the relay, the auto-off-after-print flag, and an optional delay of the printer's own. Answers 409 when another printer already has that plug and relay.

post.summary: Turn a printer's plug on or off
post.description: Switches the plug through its driver and verifies the resulting state. Refuses OFF, and a TOGGLE that would turn off, with 409 Conflict while the printer is printing or busy.

200.description: Command sent and updated plug status

post.summary: Choose whether a printer turns off after a print
post.description: With enabled alone, arms or disarms turning off after the print that runs now or the next one; the printer then goes back to its default. With default as well, sets whether the printer turns off after every print.

config.description: The saved plug, with secrets left out

plug.description: The live state and readings of the plug, absent for a printer with no plug
